content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Payments volume is well above forecast (+71% in the 11:00 interval, +46% on the alert), driven mainly by upi_payment_failed calls at 2.2x normal (+103 excess calls), with payment_status_enquiry at 1.38x. Payments AHT is normal, so this is a demand problem, not slowness. Absences are at usual levels (3 vs about 2.8 and 2.5), and no marketing entries exist. The only incident is an unrelated P4 on the HR portal. The UPI pattern looks like an upstream UPI or payment-gateway problem, but no incident confirms it, so the cause is unknown. General has only a small volume rise (+4%), but its service level is falling because it runs about 3 agents below plan and AHT is somewhat elevated. Escalate to IT to check UPI health; if an outage is confirmed, an outage message becomes possible.","plan_name":"Payments UPI surge containment with capacity protection on both queues","rationale":"Neither queue is near 70% service level, so cross-skilled moves are not allowed. Capacity has to come from free and paid levers instead. 1) Delay breaks on both queues across the late-morning peak, which is free capacity borrowed from later. 2) Cancel non-mandatory coaching to put agents back on phones. 3) Use staggered overtime offers on payments to cover the surge, plus a smaller offer on general. With about 40% acceptance, expected overtime cost is about Rs 11,500, within the Rs 15,000 budget. 4) Turn on IVR callback on payments to flatten queue peaks and cut abandons. 5) Deflect up to 20% of payment_status_enquiry calls to chat for about Rs 1,600.
